bottom_line: In COMET, all-cause mortality was 34% (512 of 1511) for carvedilol and 40% (600 of 1518) for metoprolol (hazard ratio 0.83 [95% CI 0.74–0.93], p=0.0017).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population (3029 patients), carvedilol was associated with lower all-cause mortality than metoprolol (hazard ratio 0.83 [95% CI 0.74–0.93]). However, they do not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in the composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission (0.94 [0.86–1.02], p=0.122) or in admissions alone (0.97 [0.89–1.05], p=0.45) based on the reported results.

major_points.text: Multicentre, double-blind, randomised parallel-group trial comparing carvedilol vs metoprolol tartrate in chronic heart failure.
major_points.quote: In a multicentre, double-blind, and randomised parallel group trial, we assigned 1511 patients with chronic heart failure to treatment with carvedilol (target dose 25 mg twice daily) and 1518 to metoprolol (metoprolol tartrate, target dose 50 mg twice daily).

major_points.text: Patients had symptomatic chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV) with reduced ejection fraction and prior cardiovascular admission.
major_points.quote: Patients were required to have chronic heart failure (NYHA II–IV), previous admission for a cardio-vascular reason, an ejection fraction of less than 0·35

major_points.text: The primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and the composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission; analysis was intention-to-treat.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoints were all-cause mortality and the composite endpoint of all-cause mortality or all-cause admission. Analysis was done by intention to treat.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with carvedilol than metoprolol (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.74–0.93).
major_points.quote: The all-cause mortality was 34% (512 of 1511) for carvedilol and 40% (600 of 1518) for metoprolol (hazard ratio 0·83 [95% CI 0·74–0·93], p=0·0017).

major_points.text: The composite endpoint of death or all-cause admission was not statistically significant between groups (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.86–1.02).
major_points.quote: The composite endpoint of mortality or all-cause admission occurred in 1116 (74%) of 1511 on carvedilol and in 1160 (76%) of 1518 on metoprolol (0·94 [0·86–1·02], p=0·122).

major_points.text: Reported side-effects and drug withdrawals were broadly similar between groups; some adverse events differed (e.g., hypotension).
major_points.quote: Hypotension was reported in 215 (14%) patients in the carvedilol group and in 160 (11%) patients in the metoprolol group.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were men or women with symptomatic chronic heart failure (New York Heart Association [NYHA] class II–IV)

inclusion_criteria.text: At least one cardiovascular admission during the previous 2 years.
inclusion_criteria.quote: at least one cardiovascular admission during the previous 2 years

inclusion_criteria.text: On stable heart failure treatment with ACE inhibitors for at least 4 weeks unless contraindicated.
inclusion_criteria.quote: on stable heart failure treatment with ACE inhibitors for at least 4 weeks unless contraindicated

inclusion_criteria.quote: and on treatment with diuretics (40 mg of frusemide or equivalent) for at least 2 weeks.

exclusion_criteria.text: Recent change of treatment (introduction of a new class of drug for heart failure) or treatment with oral beta-adrenergic or alpha-adrenergic receptor blockers within 2 weeks before randomisation.
